verdict.rationale: Honcho's docs describe workspaces as top-level containers that isolate applications or environments, and peers that model users and agents. Retrieval can be shaped with peer scoping, and named-scope API keys bind a key to a single scope for recall and ingestion, which covers per-user, per-agent and per-application scoping. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that peer-scoped retrieval guarantees no cross-tenant leakage inside a workspace, detailed docs on how isolation is enforced, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can scope memories per user, agent, or application so one tenant's memories never leak into another's retrieval

citations.quote: Workspaces - Top-level containers that isolate different applications or environments
Shape retrieval with search, token budgets, summaries, and peer scoping.
It enables agents to build and maintain state about any entity—users, agents, groups, ideas, and more.
Named-scope API keys: a key bound to one named scope, for recall and for message ingestion
